elements.evidence: "Ono shall have the right to terminate this Agreement at any time during the Term ... for any reasons"

elements.element: Notice period of 30 days' written notice
elements.evidence: "by giving ninety (90) days' advance written notice to Array"

elements.element: Pro-rata refund of prepaid fees on convenience termination
elements.evidence: No refund language anywhere in the redlined clause; 13.2 addresses only notice and rationale

elements.element: Vendor (Array) has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term
elements.evidence: Array's only termination rights shown are for cause: "If Ono Commercializes a Competing Product ... Array may immediately terminate"; no Array at-will right is created

elements.element: Early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees
elements.evidence: No early-termination fee is imposed on Ono; condition demonstrably absent

elements.element: Vendor convenience termination only at end of a term and only on 90 days' notice
elements.evidence: No Array convenience right exists; "Array terminates this Agreement for Ono's breach pursuant to Section 13.3" is cause-based

offending_extra_words: at any time during the Term
in its entirety or on a Product-by-Product or country-by-country basis
reasons: Locked target is preferred, but the redline lands at the fallback: notice is ninety (90) days rather than 30, and no pro-rata refund of prepaid fees is added.

Minimality fails: the operation rewrites the whole operative sentence (changed-character ratio 0.824 against the 0.600 official limit). Deleting the commencement trigger and inserting a notice number would suffice; the added scope language ('in its entirety or on a Product-by-Product or country-by-country basis') is unrequested new commercial scope, not needed to complete either level.

'the Term' is not a defined term in the supplied definitions (Section 13.1 is captioned 'Term' but defines duration by reference to the Secondary Royalty Term), so the insertion introduces an undefined reference and a dangling mechanic.

Note the preserved cross-reference in the competing-product covenant to Ono terminating 'at will' pursuant to Section 13.2 'during the Initial Royalty Term'; broadening 13.2 to pre-launch periods leaves that non-compete trigger effective but no longer coextensive with the new right — worth confirming rather than leaving unaddressed.
Vendor-side element is satisfied by absence: no Array convenience right is created, so no cure is required there.
